newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EP committee reinstates water pesticides limit.
newsitem.headline: EP committee reinstates water pesticides limit.

text.p: The European Union must not scrap the cumulative limit for pesticides in water when it revises the 1980 drinking water directive, the European Parliament's environment committee said on Thursday.

A European Commission proposal to revise the directive -- COM(94)612 -- retains the existing limit of 0.1 microgrammes of pesticide per litre for individual pesticides but scraps the 0.5 microgrammes per litre cumulative total.
The Commission has said the decision is based on advice from the CSTE scientific committee.
But the parliament's environment committee approved a report by its British Socialist chairman Ken Collins which insists the cumulative ceiling must be reinstated.
The report insists the EU must not relax its pressure on member states to clean up water supplies, especially in the light of their dismal record of compliance with the existing directive.

Collins cites European Environmental Agency figures which show that pesticides limits in drinking water have been exceeded on 75 percent of the EU's arable land, and point to an increase in nitrates in over 66 percent of the EU's rivers and most of its lakes.

One of the Commission's main proposals for improving drinking water quality is an 80 percent cut in the permitted lead content, mostly from replacing lead pipes and fittings at an estimated cost to the member states of over 50 billion Ecus.

Collins suggests funds should be made available from the Structural Funds for certain regions to help them foot the bill. But they should have 10 years to bring their water up to scratch not 15 as proposed by the Commission.
Unlike the Commission, Collins does not believe governments should be able to force individual householders to replace lead pipes on their property.
Instead, he thinks they should report to the Commission "on the incidence of lead piping in households and come forward within five years with a plan to replace the lead piping in these homes".
The proposal is one of two analyses of water policy which the parliament plans to consider at its December 9-13 plenary session under the cooperation procedure.
The other, a Commission proposal to clean up Europe's bathing waters -- COM(94)36, was also adopted by the environment committee on Thursday.
The two proposals are "daughter directives" to a planned framework directive on the EU's overall water policy, which the parliament approved in October.
